classes.name: TDataStd
classes.summary:
This package defines standard attributes for modelling. These allow you to create and modify labels and attributes for many basic data types. {@link Standard | `Standard`} topological and visualization attributes have also been created. To find an attribute attached to a specific label, you use the GUID of the type of attribute you are looking for.
To do this, first find this information using the method GetID as follows: {@link Standard_GUID | `Standard_GUID`} anID = MyAttributeClass::GetID(); Then, use the method Find for the label as follows: bool HasAttribute = aLabel.Find(anID,anAttribute); Note For information on the relations between this component of OCAF and the others, refer to the OCAF User's Guide.

classes.name: TDataStd_ChildNodeIterator
classes.summary: Iterates on the ChildStepren step of a step, at the first level only. It is possible to ask the iterator to explore all the sub step levels of the given one, with the option "allLevels".

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.comment: Iterates on the ChildStepren of the given Step. If <allLevels> option is set to true, it explores not only the first, but all the sub Step levels.

instanceMethods.name: Initialize
instanceMethods.comment: Initializes the iteration on the Children Step of the given Step. If <allLevels> option is set to true, it explores not only the first, but all the sub Step levels.

instanceMethods.name: More
instanceMethods.comment: Returns True if there is a current Item in the iteration.

instanceMethods.name: Next
instanceMethods.comment: Move to the next Item.

instanceMethods.name: NextBrother
instanceMethods.comment: Move to the next Brother. If there is none, go up etc. This method is interesting only with "allLevels" behavior, because it avoids to explore the current Step ChildStepren.

instanceMethods.name: Value
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the current item; a null Step if there is no one.

instanceMethods.name: Append
instanceMethods.comment: Insert the TreeNode <Child> as last child of <me>. If the insertion is successful <me> becomes the Father of <Child>.

instanceMethods.name: Prepend
instanceMethods.comment: Insert the the TreeNode <Child> as first child of <me>. If the insertion is successful <me> becomes the Father of <Child>.

instanceMethods.name: InsertBefore
instanceMethods.comment: Inserts the TreeNode <Node> before <me>. If insertion is successful <me> and <Node> belongs to the same Father.

instanceMethods.name: InsertAfter
instanceMethods.comment: Inserts the TreeNode <Node> after <me>. If insertion is successful <me> and <Node> belongs to the same Father.

instanceMethods.name: Remove
instanceMethods.comment: Removes this tree node attribute from its father node. The result is that this attribute becomes a root node.

instanceMethods.name: Depth
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the depth of this tree node in the overall tree node structure. In other words, the number of father tree nodes of this one is returned.

instanceMethods.name: NbChildren
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the number of child nodes. If <allLevels> is true, the method counts children of all levels (children of children ...).

instanceMethods.name: IsAscendant
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute is an ascendant of of. In other words, if it is a father or the father of a father of of.

instanceMethods.name: IsDescendant
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute is a descendant of of. In other words, if it is a child or the child of a child of of.

instanceMethods.name: IsRoot
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute is the ultimate father in the tree.

instanceMethods.name: Root
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the ultimate father of this tree node attribute.

instanceMethods.name: IsFather
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute is a father of of.

instanceMethods.name: IsChild
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute is a child of of.

instanceMethods.name: HasFather
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute has a father tree node.

instanceMethods.name: Father
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the father TreeNode of <me>. Null if root.

instanceMethods.name: HasNext
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute has a next tree node.

instanceMethods.name: Next
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the next tree node in this tree node attribute. Warning This tree node is null if it is the last one in this tree node attribute.Returns the next TreeNode of <me>. Null if last.

instanceMethods.name: HasPrevious
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute has a previous tree node.

instanceMethods.name: Previous
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the previous tree node of this tree node attribute. Warning This tree node is null if it is the first one in this tree node attribute.

instanceMethods.name: HasFirst
instanceMethods.comment: Returns true if this tree node attribute has a first child tree node.

classes.name: TDataStd_Variable
classes.summary:
**Variable attribute.**
- A variable is associated to a {@link TDataStd_Real | `TDataStd_Real`} (which contains its current value) and a {@link TDataStd_Name | `TDataStd_Name`} attribute (which contains its name). It contains a constant flag, and a Unit
- An expression may be assigned to a variable. In thatcase the expression is handled by the associated Expression Attribute and the Variable returns True to the method <IsAssigned>.
